record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: Let f: C^n -> V be a proper finite morphism from affine n-space onto a normal affine variety V. Must V be contractible?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM. Let f : Cn → V be a proper (that is, a ﬁnite) morphism from the aﬃne n-space onto a normal aﬃne variety V. Show that V is contractible.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $n \geq 1$ and let $f : \mathbb{C}^n \to V$ be a proper (equivalently, finite) surjective morphism from complex affine $n$-space onto a normal complex affine algebraic variety $V$. Prove that $V$ is contractible (as a topological space with its usual Euclidean topology), or exhibit a counterexample.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not produce a definitive resolution. The problem appears in lists of challenging open problems on affine n-space (Montreal 1994 and subsequent surveys). For n = 2 the answer is known to be yes (V is a quotient C^2/G by a small finite subgroup of GL(2,C), hence contractible), but in general dimensions no clear published resolution was found.

status_evidence.title: Challenging problems on affine n-space
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open problems on affine n-space, including questions about finite/proper images of C^n.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is listed among open challenging problems on affine n-space.

status_evidence.title: On the compactifications of contractible affine threefolds and the Zariski Cancellation Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses contractible affine varieties and related open problems in affine algebraic geometry.
status_evidence.claim: Contractibility questions for affine varieties remain an active area without complete resolution in higher dimension.
